### 1. What the user expresses; simulator behaviour

- Target object: "a collection account with you for my old Buckeye Federal card"; aim: "I want to pay as much as you'll take today on it. Whatever the most is, that's what I want to do."
- Channel boundary stated early on his own initiative: "anything coming out of your checking account you would rather do yourself on Ridgeline's website, because you do not like reading your bank details over the phone."
- Payment means stated only when asked: "you have your debit card and a Visa credit card right in front of you, plus the checking account."
- Authorisation mode: for cards, "If the agent tells you an amount they can take on one of your cards and asks whether to go ahead, you say yes and let them run it"; for the bank payment, he runs it himself once the agent "has set up the bank payment on the website for you and gives you the account reference and the amount".
- The simulator is passive: it conveys the need, answers what is asked, approves each card amount, and executes the one user tool the agent hands over. It does not volunteer an order or amounts ("you have no figure of your own in mind").

### 2. Act now / wait / refuse

Act now, in three writes on 2026-10-08. Visible eligibility grounds:
- Account status `active` (find_placed_accounts) — "A consumer payment is posted only to an account whose status is placed, validation period, active, arranged, dispute hold or hardship hold" (Cashiering Standard §1).
- Stage `Secondary Placement`: "Credit cards accepted: Yes" (Payment Schedule, Channel availability); ACH bank debit and debit card accepted at every stage (Cashiering Standard §2).
- No electronic-channel block: one returned payment (2026-07-24) in the 180-day counting window; Secondary trigger is 2 (Returned-Payment Block Settings).
- Minimum payment $10.00 (Secondary) — every derived amount is above it.
- The retired clauses ("(retired) A single card payment ... may not exceed ...", "(retired) A single ACH payment may not exceed ...") are marked "no longer in force" and are not applied as caps; the stage maxima enter only through the ceilings.

### 4. Scored parameters

**(a) Phone debit-card payment = debit-card ceiling of the day** (Debit-Card Ceiling Calculation Sheet + its four ladders).
- Rolling limit — Risk Table "Debit-Card Rolling Limit After Returned Payments": returns in last six months = 1 (07-24) → "$2400.00 for an account with exactly one returned payment".
- Plan-standing percentage — "Plan Standing and the Debit-Card Ceiling": plan carries broken date 2026-08-26; missed-installment entries in last six months = 2 (07-26, 08-26) → "75% where any payment plan on the account carries a broken date and 2 or more missed installments ..." → 2400.00 × 75% = 1800.00 ("the rolling limit is multiplied by the plan-standing percentage, and the percentage applies to no other amount").
- Track-record allowance — "Card Track-Record Allowance on the Debit-Card Ceiling": card payments in last three months = 4 (08-31, 09-14, 09-29 debit; 10-02 credit; 07-06 is out); no card payment ever returned (only return is ACH) → "$500.00 where 3 or more card payments ..." ; "added, at its full amount, to the amount from which the payments counted ... are subtracted".
- Payments counted — "Payments Counted Against the Debit-Card Ceiling": credit-card payment in last month yes (10-02); bank-debit payment in last three months yes (07-20, "counts at its posted amount whether or not it was later returned") → "every card and bank-debit payment ... received in the last month": 600.00 + 250.00 + 400.00 = 1250.00 (no ACH in last month).
- Figure = 1800.00 + 500.00 − 1250.00 = 1050.00 (rounded once; already to the cent). Ceiling = min(1050.00, single card max $5000.00 [Secondary], balance due 4651.44) = **1050.00**.

**(b) Phone credit-card payment = credit-card ceiling of the day**, worked after (a) is booked (balance due 3601.44).
- Card limit — "Card Limit for Credit-Card Payments on Bank-Card Debts": bank_card, charge-off 2025-10-30, 343 calendar days before 2026-10-08 (< 730) → $4500.00.
- Plan-cancellation percentage — "Plans Closed as Broken and Not Reinstated": most recent such closing 2026-09-26, fewer than 3 whole months back → 80% → 4500.00 × 80% = 3600.00 ("the percentage applies to the card limit alone").
- Hardship cushion — "Hardship Cushion on Credit-Card Payments": Documented Hardship Hold ended 2026-04-15, inside the six months (from 04-09) → $150.00, subtracted.
- Payments counted — "Card Payments Counted Against the Credit-Card Ceiling": returned payment in last six months yes (07-24) and card payment in last month yes → "every card payment, debit or credit, received in the last two months": 150.00 (08-31) + 600.00 + 250.00 + 400.00 + 1050.00 (today's phone debit-card payment) = 2450.00.
- Figure = 3600.00 − 150.00 − 2450.00 = 1000.00. Ceiling = min(1000.00, $5000.00, 3601.44) = **1000.00**.

**(c) Portal bank-debit payment = portal bank-debit ceiling of the day**, worked after (b) is booked (balance due 2601.44).
- Limit — "Portal Bank-Debit Limit by Return Reason": an `account_closed` return in last six months (07-24) → $3000.00.
- Same-day payments counted — "Same-Day Payments Counted Against the Portal Bank-Debit Limit": a plan closed "broken, not reinstated" exists → every card and bank-debit payment of the handling date: 1050.00 + 1000.00 = 2050.00.
- Retest percentage — "Bank-Debit Retest Percentage": most recent bank-debit return 2026-07-24 is after the most recent bank-debit payment 2026-07-20 → 50%, applied to (limit − same-day counted) = 950.00 → 475.00.
- Installment-record allowance — "Installment-Record Allowance on Portal Bank-Debit Payments": 4 installment-paid entries − 1 installment-returned entry = 3 → $200.00, added.
- Figure = (3000.00 − 2050.00) × 50% + 200.00 = 675.00. Ceiling = min(675.00, single ACH max $25000.00 [Secondary], 2601.44) = **675.00**.

**Fall-back answers** (computation documents alone, with the payment-schedule figures they name):
- debit card: 10000.00 − debit-card payments of last month (600 + 250 = 850.00) = 9150.00 → min(9150.00, 5000.00, 4651.44) = 4651.44 (≠ 1050.00).
- credit card (after 4651.44 debit): balance 0 → 0.00; or, given the derived debit amount, 10000 − 400 = 9600 → min(9600, 5000, 3601.44) = 3601.44 (≠ 1000.00).
- portal bank-debit: 25000.00 − 0 → min(25000, 25000, 2601.44) = 2601.44 (≠ 675.00).

### 6. Problem tree derived from visible materials alone

Root (customer's own write): the portal bank-debit payment from his checking account ("anything coming out of your checking account you would rather do yourself on Ridgeline's website"), governed by "Payment Portal Terms ...: Paying from the Consumer's Own Bank Account": "When a consumer asks to pay the most an account will accept in one day and chooses to pay from their own bank account, the consumer makes one bank-debit payment through the payment portal equal to the portal bank-debit ceiling of the day".

- Hop 1 (portal bank-debit ← phone credit-card payment). Visible sentence in the portal bank-debit hub: "When a consumer who also offers a credit card asks to pay the most an account will accept in one day, the portal bank-debit ceiling of the day is not fixed until the day's credit-card payment has been taken by the phone desk." Records/transcript: the caller offers a Visa credit card; money history shows no credit-card payment dated 2026-10-08 (last one 10-02). The named action — a credit-card payment taken by the phone desk — is performed under "Phone Desk Guidance: Credit-Card Payments" ("When a consumer asks to pay the most an account will accept in one day and offers a credit card, at a stage that accepts credit cards, the phone desk takes one credit-card payment equal to the credit-card ceiling of the day"); Secondary accepts credit cards. Mark: **action-named**.
- Hop 2 (phone credit-card ← phone debit-card payment). Visible sentence in the phone credit-card hub: "When a consumer who also offers a debit card asks to pay the most an account will accept in one day, the credit-card ceiling of the day is fixed only after the day's debit-card payment has been taken by the phone desk." Caller offers a debit card; no debit-card payment dated 2026-10-08. The action is performed under "Phone Desk Guidance: Debit-Card Payments" ("When a consumer asks to pay the most an account will accept in one day and offers a debit card, the phone desk takes one debit-card payment equal to the debit-card ceiling of the day"). Mark: **action-named**.
- The phone debit-card hub carries no "fixed only after / not fixed until" sentence → leaf.
- Problem list and order: (1) phone debit-card payment 1050.00 (agent) → (2) phone credit-card payment 1000.00 (agent) → (3) portal bank-debit payment 675.00 (user). Dependency direction: 3 waits on 2, 2 waits on 1.
- Why the cards go by phone rather than the portal: the caller restricts only the checking-account payment to the website and agrees to "let them run" card amounts; the two waited-on actions are worded "taken by the phone desk". No hop was pre-solved: no other problem's tool name, route, chain, or ordering table appears in any hub; each hub names only its own tool.

### Two-way counter-proof

- "Do only the one thing" (portal bank payment only, 1700.00 = (3000 − 0) × 50% + 200): excluded by the portal bank-debit hub sentence — with a credit card offered, the ceiling "is not fixed until the day's credit-card payment has been taken by the phone desk"; and the customer's ask ("as much as you'll take today") is answered per channel by the three phone/portal rules, each of which applies to his offered means.
- Reversed order (credit card before debit card): excluded by "the credit-card ceiling of the day is fixed only after the day's debit-card payment has been taken by the phone desk".
- Portal cards instead of phone cards: not supported by the transcript (only the checking account is to go through the website; card amounts are run by the agent); the waited-on actions are phone-desk actions.
- Plan record `status cancelled` vs close reason: the clause reads the close reason ("Only plans closed with the close reason 'broken, not reinstated' count"); record close_reason `broken_not_reinstated` → counts (80% and same-day "every card and bank-debit payment").
- Hold end: `ended_date` 2026-04-15 is "the last day the hold covered, or the withdrawal date"; the planned end_date 2026-05-18 would give the same tier. Either way $150.00.
- The returned 07-20 ACH payment: counts in the debit-card counted test ("whether or not it was later returned"); the tier is unchanged either way (row 1 and row 2 give 1250.00).
- Card limit: 343 days < 730 → $4500.00, not $5500.00.
- Assembly of percentages and allowances: each factor doc fixes its operand ("applies to no other amount", "to that difference and to nothing else", "added, at its full amount"), so one assembly only.
